avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 induction reduces theophylline levels and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; monitor theophylline levels if discontinuation occurs

avoid_supplements.name: Echinacea
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May induce CYP1A2 and CYP3A4, potentially reducing theophylline concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Use cautiously; monitor for reduced bronchodilator effectiveness

caution_supplements.name: Grapeseed extract
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential mild CYP3A4 inhibition may increase theophylline levels
caution_supplements.action: Monitor theophylline serum concentrations if used concurrently

caution_supplements.name: Licorice root
caution_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate CNS stimulation effects of theophylline
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; counsel on potential increased nervousness or tremor

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit/grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases theophylline bioavailability and serum concentrations, raising toxicity risk
avoid_foods.action: Avoid grapefruit products entirely; substitute with other citrus fruits

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase theophylline absorption and delay peak serum concentrations
caution_foods.action: Administer theophylline consistently with or without food; avoid timing changes

caution_foods.name: Charbroiled foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons induce CYP1A2, potentially reducing theophylline levels
caution_foods.action: Maintain consistent dietary patterns; monitor efficacy if intake increases significantly

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing foods/beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Additive CNS stimulation and similar metabolism via CYP1A2; may increase adverse effects
caution_foods.action: Limit caffeine intake; counsel on potential increased jitteriness or insomnia

monitoring_notes: Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic index (10-20 mcg/mL); therapeutic drug monitoring is essential, particularly when interactions occur. Monitor for toxicity signs (nausea, tachycardia, tremor, arrhythmias) and efficacy changes, especially with CYP1A2 inducers or inhibitors.
